English Literature (Full).question: ১) ‘God of small things’ was written by -
English Literature (Full).exp:
In 1997 Arundhati Roy published her debut novel, The God of Small Things to wide acclaim.
The semi-autobiographical work departed from the conventional plots and light prose that had been typical among best-sellers.

English Literature (Full).question: ২) Who is the author of ‘India Wins Freedom’?
English Literature (Full).exp:
'India Wins Freedom' এর রচয়িতা ব্রিটিশ বিরোধী আন্দোলনের বিখ্যাত নেতা মাওলানা আবুল কালাম আাজাদ।

English Literature (Full).question: ৩) ‘Robinson Crusoe’ was written by -
English Literature (Full).exp:
Robinson Crusoe, novel by Daniel Defoe, first published in London in 1719.
Defoe’s first long work of fiction, it introduced two of the most-enduring characters in English literature: Robinson Crusoe and Friday.
[Source: Britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ৪) ‘September on Jessore Road’ is written by -
English Literature (Full).exp:
September on Jessore Road is a poem by Allen Ginsberg on refugees from Bangladesh Liberation war in 1971.
During Bangladesh's Liberation War in 1971, the US government was an ally of Pakistan and even sent its 7th fleet to intimidate India from interfering with the events in then East Pakistan.
Source: The New York Times.

English Literature (Full).question: ৫) The author of the book ‘Asian Drama’ is -
English Literature (Full).exp:
The book Asian Drama: An Inquiry into the Poverty of Nations (1968) represents a 10-year study of poverty in Asia is written by Gunnar Myrdal.
[Source: Britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ৬) A serious play with a sad ending is called a -
English Literature (Full).exp:
Tragedy, branch of drama that treats in a serious and dignified style the sorrowful or terrible events encountered or caused by a heroic individual.
[Source: Britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ৭) The period from AD 1660 to 1798 is known as -
English Literature (Full).exp:
The Neo-classical period (1660-1798) is divided into three periods. Such as
1. The Restoration Period (1660-1700),
2. The Augustan Age or the Age of Pope (1700-1745) and
3. The Age of Sensibility or The Age of Johnson (1745-1798).
And, the Elizabethan Period is from 1558 to 1603 ;
Jacobean Period is from 1603 to 1625.
[Source: Live MCQ lecture.]

English Literature (Full).question: ৮) Who wrote Prometheus Bound?
English Literature (Full).exp:
Prometheus Bound, Greek Promētheus desmōtēs, tragedy by Aeschylus, the dating of which is uncertain.
The play concerns the god Prometheus, who in defiance of Zeus (Jupiter) has saved humanity with his gift of fire.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ৯) A work which has a meaning behind the surface meaning is -
English Literature (Full).exp:
Allegory is a literary form in which one story is told in the guise of another story.
In other words, an allegory is a story of double meanings.
Allegory, a symbolic fictional narrative that conveys a meaning not explicitly set forth in the narrative.
Allegory, which encompasses such forms as fable, parable, and apologue, may have meaning on two or more levels that the reader can understand only through an interpretive process.
[Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ১০) Pearl S. Buck awarded Nobel Prize for the book -
English Literature (Full).exp:
Pearl S. Buck is an American novelist and writer.
She was awarded the Nobel prize in 1938 for her rich and truly epic description of peasant life in China.
Pearl S. Buck was the first American woman to win the Nobel prize for literature.
Source: Live MCQ lecture.

English Literature (Full).question: ১১) ‘For God’s sake hold your tongue, and let me love.’ this line is written by -
English Literature (Full).exp:
‘For God’s sake hold your tongue, and let me love.’ - it is a famous quotation by John Donne.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature (Full).exp:
Charles Dickense's famous novel:

- A Christmas Carol
- David Copperfield
- Bleak House
- Great Expectations Almost in his every creation, he set a plot for London city.

English Literature (Full).question: ১৩) The short story ‘The Diamond Necklace’ was written by -
English Literature (Full).exp:
The Necklace or 'The Diamond Necklace' is a short story by French writer Guy de Maupassant.
It is known for its twist ending, which was a hallmark of Maupassant's style.

English Literature (Full).question: ১৪) What is the real name of George Eliot?
English Literature (Full).exp:
George Eliot (1819 – 80):
- Born at Arbury Form, Warwickshire.
- Real name – Mary Ann Evans.
- Major Works: Adam Bede (1859), The Mill on the Floss, Middlemarch, Romola, Silas Marner etc.
Source: Brittanica.com

English Literature (Full).question: ১৫) Who wrote Old Man and the Sea?
English Literature (Full).exp:
The Old Man and the Sea, short heroic novel by Ernest Hemingway, published in 1952 and awarded the 1953 Pulitzer Prize for fiction.
It was his last major work of fiction. The story centres on an aging fisherman who engages in an epic battle to catch a giant marlin.
[source : Britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ১৬) Author of ‘The Time Machine’ is –
English Literature (Full).exp:
‘The Time Machine’ H. G. Wells রচিত একটি বিখ্যাত science fiction.
তার পুরো নাম - Herbert George Wells.
তার রচিত উল্লেখযোগ্য আরো কয়েকটি সায়েন্স ফিকশান - The Invisible Man, The War of the Worlds, The Island of Doctor Moreau, The First Men in the Moon ইত্যাদি।
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ১৭) The author of ‘Road to freedom’ is -
English Literature (Full).exp:
Bertrand Russell was British philosopher, logician, mathematician, history writer, social critic and political activist.
He was awarded the Nobel prize in literature in 1950.
Famous writings of Russell: The elements of ethics, Human knowledge, Road to freedom, Authority and Individual, Marriage and Morals, Religion and Science etc.
'The Roads to Freedom' novel series is by Jean-Paul Sartre,
'Proposed Roads to Freedom' is by Bertrand Russell.

English Literature (Full).question: ১৮) Who wrote the book ‘To the lighthouse’?
English Literature (Full).exp:
To the Lighthouse, novel by Virginia Woolf, published in 1927.
The work is one of her most successful and accessible experiments in the stream-of-consciousness style.
The three sections of the book take place between 1910 and 1920 and revolve around various members of the Ramsay family during visits to their summer residence on the Isle of Skye in Scotland.
[Source: britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ১৯) Who wrote the novel ‘A Passage to India’?
English Literature (Full).exp:
A Passage to India, novel by E.M. Forster published in 1924 and considered one of the author’s finest works.
The novel examines racism and colonialism.
[Source: Britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ২০) Who is the greatest modern English dramatist?
English Literature (Full).exp:
George Bernard Shaw is the greatest modern English dramatist who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1925.
[Source: britannica]

English Literature (Full).question: ২১) ‘Animal Farm’ is a famous novel by -
English Literature (Full).exp:
George Orwell (1903 – 1989):
English novelist, essayist, journalist and critic.
His real name is Eric Hugh Blair. He was a police officer in Burma.
Works: Novel: Animal Farm (1945 – a fairy story), Nineteen Eighty-Four, Burmese Days, Coming up for Air.
Story/Essay: Shooting an Elephant, A Hanging.
Source: Britannica

English Literature (Full).question: ২২) Who is the author of the book ‘War and Peace’?

War and Peace is a historical novel by Leo Tolstoy.

This intense, solidly imagined novel is distinguished from other novels of the period by its dramatic and poetic presentation, its abstention from authorial intrusion, and its unusual structure.

English Literature (Full).question: ২৮) Identify the poet of the verse: ‘Our sweetest songs are those that tell of saddest thought’.

We look before and after,
And pine for what is not:
Our sincerest laughter With some pain is fraught;

Endymion,
Hyperion,
Lamia,
Ode to a Nightingale,
Ode to Autumn,
The Eve of St. Agnes,

Heaven and Earth.

Thomas Kyd, John Lyly, Robert Greene, George Peele, Christopher Marlowe and Thomas Nashe are university wits.

[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]
